under-explored. Thus, this research investigates the human behavior in
determining table unionability within data discovery. We have designed an
experimental survey and conducted a comprehensive analysis, in which we assess
human decision-making for table unionability. We use the observations from the
analysis to develop a machine learning framework to boost the (raw) performance
of humans. Furthermore, we perform a preliminary study on how LLM performance
is compared to humans indicating that it is typically better to consider a
combination of both. We believe that this work lays the foundations for
developing future Human-in-the-Loop systems for efficient data discovery.

</details>


<div id='hep-ex'></div>

# hep-ex [[Back]](#toc)

### [395] [eLog analysis for accelerators: status and future outlook](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12949)
*Antonin Sulc,Thorsten Hellert,Aaron Reed,Adam Carpenter,Alex Bien,Chris Tennant,Claudio Bisegni,Daniel Lersch,Daniel Ratner,David Lawrence,Diana McSpadden,Hayden Hoschouer,Jason St. John,Thomas Britton*

Main category: hep-ex

TL;DR: This paper explores the use of AI-driven electronic logbook (eLog) systems at several accelerator facilities, evaluating tools and methodologies for information retrieval using Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAGs). It addresses challenges in eLog analysis, presents practical implementations, and proposes a framework to enhance operations through better information accessibility and knowledge management.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To improve the efficiency and effectiveness of operations at accelerator facilities by leveraging modern AI technologies for information retrieval and knowledge management in electronic logbooks.

Method: Evaluation of contemporary tools and methodologies for information retrieval with Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAGs), focusing on operational insights and integration with existing accelerator control systems.

Result: The study demonstrates applications and limitations of state-of-the-art eLog analysis through practical implementations, presenting a framework for enhancing accelerator facility operations.

Conclusion: Enhancing information accessibility and knowledge management through improved eLog systems could potentially lead to more efficient operations at accelerator facilities.

Abstract: This work demonstrates electronic logbook (eLog) systems leveraging modern
AI-driven information retrieval capabilities at the accelerator facilities of
Fermilab, Jefferson Lab, Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL), SLAC
National Accelerator Laboratory. We evaluate contemporary tools and
methodologies for information retrieval with Retrieval Augmented Generation
(RAGs), focusing on operational insights and integration with existing
accelerator control systems.
  The study addresses challenges and proposes solutions for state-of-the-art
eLog analysis through practical implementations, demonstrating applications and
limitations. We present a framework for enhancing accelerator facility
operations through improved information accessibility and knowledge management,
which could potentially lead to more efficient operations.

</details>


<div id='stat.ML'></div>

# stat.ML [[Back]](#toc)

### [396] [On the existence of consistent adversarial attacks in high-dimensional linear classification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12454)
*Matteo Vilucchio,Lenka Zdeborová,Bruno Loureiro*

Main category: stat.ML

TL;DR: The paper explores the distinction between adversarial attacks and misclassifications in high-dimensional binary classification, introducing a new error metric to quantify model vulnerability to label-preserving adversarial attacks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To understand what fundamentally distinguishes adversarial attacks from misclassifications due to limited model expressivity or finite data in high-dimensional binary classification.

Method: Investigation of high-dimensional binary classification setting with introduction of a new error metric that captures the distinction between adversarial attacks and misclassifications. Rigorous asymptotic characterization of these metrics is provided for both well-specified models and latent space models.

Result: Exact and rigorous asymptotic characterization of the new error metric shows different vulnerability patterns compared to standard robust error measures. More overparameterized models are more vulnerable to label-preserving perturbations.

Conclusion: As models become more overparameterized, their vulnerability to label-preserving adversarial attacks increases, providing theoretical insight into model sensitivity to such attacks.

Abstract: What fundamentally distinguishes an adversarial attack from a
misclassification due to limited model expressivity or finite data? In this
work, we investigate this question in the setting of high-dimensional binary
classification, where statistical effects due to limited data availability play
a central role. We introduce a new error metric that precisely capture this
distinction, quantifying model vulnerability to consistent adversarial attacks
-- perturbations that preserve the ground-truth labels. Our main technical
contribution is an exact and rigorous asymptotic characterization of these
metrics in both well-specified models and latent space models, revealing
different vulnerability patterns compared to standard robust error measures.
The theoretical results demonstrate that as models become more
overparameterized, their vulnerability to label-preserving perturbations grows,
offering theoretical insight into the mechanisms underlying model sensitivity
to adversarial attacks.

</details>


### [397] [Theoretical Tensions in RLHF: Reconciling Empirical Success with Inconsistencies in Social Choice Theory](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12350)
*Jiancong Xiao,Zhekun Shi,Kaizhao Liu,Qi Long,Weijie J. Su*

Main category: stat.ML

TL;DR: 尽管强化学习在实践中表现良好，但它违反了社会选择理论中的基本公理。本文通过实证假设解释了这一矛盾，并提出了改进奖励模型目标的 slight modification 来确保一致性，同时引入新的对齐标准以更好地反映学习响应分布的目标。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 研究旨在解释为什么强化学习在违反社会选择理论基本公理的情况下仍然在实践中表现出色。

Method: 通过展示在实际假设下的偏好配置文件中，RLHF 满足成对多数和孔多赛一致性。提出对奖励建模目标的 slight modification 以确保一般偏好配置文件下的一致性。引入新的对齐标准：偏好匹配、偏好等价和群体偏好匹配。

Result: 证明 RLHF 在实际假设下满足成对多数和孔多赛一致性，并且满足前两个新标准但不满足第三个标准。

Conclusion: 未来的研究可以通过设计满足所有三个新标准的方法来进一步改善对齐过程。

Abstract: Despite its empirical success, Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
(RLHF) has been shown to violate almost all the fundamental axioms in social
choice theory -- such as majority consistency, pairwise majority consistency,
and Condorcet consistency. This raises a foundational question: why does RLHF
perform so well in practice if it fails these seemingly essential properties?
In this paper, we resolve this paradox by showing that under mild and
empirically plausible assumptions on the preference profile, RLHF does satisfy
pairwise majority and Condorcet consistency. These assumptions are frequently
satisfied in real-world alignment tasks, offering a theoretical explanation for
RLHF's strong practical performance. Furthermore, we show that a slight
modification to the reward modeling objective can ensure pairwise majority or
Condorcet consistency even under general preference profiles, thereby improving
the alignment process. Finally, we go beyond classical axioms in economic and
social choice theory and introduce new alignment criteria -- preference
matching, preference equivalence, and group preference matching -- that better
reflect the goal of learning distributions over responses. We show that while
RLHF satisfies the first two properties, it fails to satisfy the third. We
conclude by discussing how future alignment methods may be designed to satisfy
all three.

</details>


### [398] [Temporal cross-validation impacts multivariate time series subsequence anomaly detection evaluation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12183)
*Steven C. Hespeler,Pablo Moriano,Mingyan Li,Samuel C. Hollifield*

Main category: stat.ML

TL;DR: This paper explores the impact of time series cross-validation (TSCV) strategies on classifier performance for detecting anomalies in multivariate time series data. It compares walk-forward and sliding window methods, finding that sliding windows generally improve precision-recall characteristics, especially for deep learning models.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing techniques for evaluating anomaly detection in multivariate time series do not adequately explore how time series cross-validation affects classifier performance, particularly in fault detection scenarios.

Method: The study systematically evaluates two TSCV strategies - walk-forward and sliding window - across various configurations and classifiers (shallow learners and deep learning). It examines their influence on precision-recall characteristics in detecting fault-like anomalies.

Result: Sliding window TSCV consistently provides higher median AUC-PR scores and less variance in performance compared to walk-forward, particularly benefiting deep learning models. Classifier generalization depends on partitioning strategy, with overlapping windows preserving fault signatures better at lower fold counts.

Conclusion: TSCV design significantly impacts the evaluation of anomaly detection models in temporally structured data, providing guidance for selecting appropriate strategies.

Abstract: Evaluating anomaly detection in multivariate time series (MTS) requires
careful consideration of temporal dependencies, particularly when detecting
subsequence anomalies common in fault detection scenarios. While time series
cross-validation (TSCV) techniques aim to preserve temporal ordering during
model evaluation, their impact on classifier performance remains underexplored.
This study systematically investigates the effect of TSCV strategy on the
precision-recall characteristics of classifiers trained to detect fault-like
anomalies in MTS datasets. We compare walk-forward (WF) and sliding window (SW)
methods across a range of validation partition configurations and classifier
types, including shallow learners and deep learning (DL) classifiers. Results
show that SW consistently yields higher median AUC-PR scores and reduced
fold-to-fold performance variance, particularly for deep architectures
sensitive to localized temporal continuity. Furthermore, we find that
classifier generalization is sensitive to the number and structure of temporal
partitions, with overlapping windows preserving fault signatures more
effectively at lower fold counts. A classifier-level stratified analysis
reveals that certain algorithms, such as random forests (RF), maintain stable
performance across validation schemes, whereas others exhibit marked
sensitivity. This study demonstrates that TSCV design in benchmarking anomaly
detection models on streaming time series and provide guidance for selecting
evaluation strategies in temporally structured learning environments.

</details>


### [399] [A Transfer Learning Framework for Multilayer Networks via Model Averaging](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12455)
*Yongqin Qiu,Xinyu Zhang*

Main category: stat.ML

TL;DR: The paper introduces a novel transfer learning framework for link prediction in multilayer networks using a bi-level model averaging method.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing techniques for link prediction in multilayer networks often rely on assumptions about shared structures and require access to raw auxiliary data, which limits their practicality.

Method: A transfer learning framework is proposed that uses a bi-level model averaging method. A K-fold cross-validation criterion based on edges is used to automatically weight inter-layer and intra-layer candidate models, enabling information transfer from auxiliary layers while mitigating model uncertainty without prior knowledge of shared structures.

Result: Simulations show that the method outperforms others in predictive accuracy and robustness. Its practical value is demonstrated through two real-world recommendation system applications.

Conclusion: Theoretically, the optimality and weight convergence of the method are proven under mild conditions. Computationally, the framework is efficient and privacy-preserving, avoiding raw data sharing and supporting parallel processing across multiple servers.

Abstract: Link prediction in multilayer networks is a key challenge in applications
such as recommendation systems and protein-protein interaction prediction.
While many techniques have been developed, most rely on assumptions about
shared structures and require access to raw auxiliary data, limiting their
practicality. To address these issues, we propose a novel transfer learning
framework for multilayer networks using a bi-level model averaging method. A
$K$-fold cross-validation criterion based on edges is used to automatically
weight inter-layer and intra-layer candidate models. This enables the transfer
of information from auxiliary layers while mitigating model uncertainty, even
without prior knowledge of shared structures. Theoretically, we prove the
optimality and weight convergence of our method under mild conditions.
Computationally, our framework is efficient and privacy-preserving, as it
avoids raw data sharing and supports parallel processing across multiple
servers. Simulations show our method outperforms others in predictive accuracy
and robustness. We further demonstrate its practical value through two
real-world recommendation system applications.

</details>


### [400] [Dependent Randomized Rounding for Budget Constrained Experimental Design](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12677)
*Khurram Yamin,Edward Kennedy,Bryan Wilder*

Main category: stat.ML

TL;DR: 在资源受限的情况下，通过将分配概率转换为二元处理决策来设计实验，以满足严格的预算限制并确保对处理效果的精确估计。方法保留了边缘处理概率并减少了方差，从而提高了估计精度。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 政策制定者需要在资源受限的环境中设计实验，这些实验要在严格的预算限制下确保对处理效果的精确估计。

Method: 提出了一种框架，该框架应用依赖随机舍入程序将分配概率转换为二元处理决策。此方法保留了边缘处理概率并诱导了任务间的负相关性。

Result: 建立了逆倾向加权和一般线性估计器的理论保证，并通过实证研究证明了该方法在固定预算约束下的高效性和准确性。

Conclusion: 所提出的方法能够在严格的预算限制下提供精确的处理效果估计，适用于资源受限环境中的政策制定。

Abstract: Policymakers in resource-constrained settings require experimental designs
that satisfy strict budget limits while ensuring precise estimation of
treatment effects. We propose a framework that applies a dependent randomized
rounding procedure to convert assignment probabilities into binary treatment
decisions. Our proposed solution preserves the marginal treatment probabilities
while inducing negative correlations among assignments, leading to improved
estimator precision through variance reduction. We establish theoretical
guarantees for the inverse propensity weighted and general linear estimators,
and demonstrate through empirical studies that our approach yields efficient
and accurate inference under fixed budget constraints.

</details>


### [401] [Fair Bayesian Model-Based Clustering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12839)
*Jihu Lee,Kunwoong Kim,Yongdai Kim*

Main category: stat.ML

TL;DR: 提出了一种基于公平贝叶斯聚类(FBC)的模型，解决了传统K-means方法需要提前设定聚类数量和实例距离的问题。FBC通过设计特殊的先验分布和高效的MCMC算法，能够自动推断出聚类的数量，并适用于任何定义了似然函数的数据类型。实验表明，FBC在推断聚类数、效用-公平性权衡以及处理分类数据方面表现出色。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 随着机器学习技术的发展和对可信赖AI需求的增长，公平聚类任务变得越来越重要。现有的大多数公平聚类方法依赖于K-means聚类，需要预先给出实例之间的距离和聚类数量，这限制了其灵活性和应用范围。

Method: 提出了一种名为公平贝叶斯聚类(FBC)的方法。该方法开发了一个专门设计的先验分布，使其质量仅集中在公平聚类上，并实现了一个高效的马尔科夫链蒙特卡洛(MCMC)算法。这种方法可以推断出聚类的数量，并且只要定义了似然函数，就可以应用于任何数据类型（例如分类数据）。

Result: 实验证明，FBC (i) 能够合理地推断出聚类的数量；(ii) 在与现有公平聚类方法相比时，实现了具有竞争力的效用-公平性权衡；(iii) 在分类数据上的表现良好。

Conclusion: 公平贝叶斯聚类(FBC)是一种有效的新型聚类方法，它不仅能够自动推断聚类数量，还能够在效用和公平性之间取得良好的平衡，并且适用于多种数据类型。

Abstract: Fair clustering has become a socially significant task with the advancement
of machine learning technologies and the growing demand for trustworthy AI.
Group fairness ensures that the proportions of each sensitive group are similar
in all clusters. Most existing group-fair clustering methods are based on the
$K$-means clustering and thus require the distance between instances and the
number of clusters to be given in advance. To resolve this limitation, we
propose a fair Bayesian model-based clustering called Fair Bayesian Clustering
(FBC). We develop a specially designed prior which puts its mass only on fair
clusters, and implement an efficient MCMC algorithm. Advantages of FBC are that
it can infer the number of clusters and can be applied to any data type as long
as the likelihood is defined (e.g., categorical data). Experiments on
real-world datasets show that FBC (i) reasonably infers the number of clusters,
(ii) achieves a competitive utility-fairness trade-off compared to existing
fair clustering methods, and (iii) performs well on categorical data.

</details>


### [402] [Single Index Bandits: Generalized Linear Contextual Bandits with Unknown Reward Functions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12751)
*Yue Kang,Mingshuo Liu,Bongsoo Yi,Jing Lyu,Zhi Zhang,Doudou Zhou,Yao Li*

Main category: stat.ML

TL;DR: Generalized linear bandits with unknown reward functions are studied, proposing algorithms (STOR, ESTOR, GSTOR) that achieve optimal regret bounds and perform well in experiments.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing methods for generalized linear bandits assume known expected reward functions, which is often unrealistic. Misspecification can cause algorithm failure.

Method: Introduced single index bandits problem with unknown reward functions. Proposed STOR and ESTOR algorithms for monotonically increasing reward functions, extended to high-dimensional sparse setting, and introduced GSTOR for general reward functions.

Result: ESTOR achieves nearly optimal regret bound $\tilde{O}_T(\sqrt{T})$. Methods work in high-dimensional sparse settings and GSTOR handles general reward functions with established regret bounds.

Conclusion: Proposed algorithms show efficiency and effectiveness through experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets.

Abstract: Generalized linear bandits have been extensively studied due to their broad
applicability in real-world online decision-making problems. However, these
methods typically assume that the expected reward function is known to the
users, an assumption that is often unrealistic in practice. Misspecification of
this link function can lead to the failure of all existing algorithms. In this
work, we address this critical limitation by introducing a new problem of
generalized linear bandits with unknown reward functions, also known as single
index bandits. We first consider the case where the unknown reward function is
monotonically increasing, and propose two novel and efficient algorithms, STOR
and ESTOR, that achieve decent regrets under standard assumptions. Notably, our
ESTOR can obtain the nearly optimal regret bound $\tilde{O}_T(\sqrt{T})$ in
terms of the time horizon $T$. We then extend our methods to the
high-dimensional sparse setting and show that the same regret rate can be
attained with the sparsity index. Next, we introduce GSTOR, an algorithm that
is agnostic to general reward functions, and establish regret bounds under a
Gaussian design assumption. Finally, we validate the efficiency and
effectiveness of our algorithms through experiments on both synthetic and
real-world datasets.

</details>


### [403] [General and Estimable Learning Bound Unifying Covariate and Concept Shifts](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12829)
*Hongbo Chen,Li Charlie Xia*

Main category: stat.ML

TL;DR: This paper bridges the gap between theory and practical applications in generalization under distribution shift by proposing new definitions for covariate and concept shifts using entropic optimal transport, deriving a unified error bound applicable to broad loss functions, and developing estimators with guarantees along with the DataShifts algorithm.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The motivation is to address the limitations of existing learning bound theory which is restricted to idealized settings and cannot be estimated from samples, especially when dealing with distribution shifts in machine learning.

Method: The method involves leveraging entropic optimal transport to create new support-agnostic definitions for covariate and concept shifts. The authors derive a novel unified error bound that applies to various loss functions, label spaces, and stochastic labeling. They also develop estimators for these shifts with concentration guarantees and introduce the DataShifts algorithm.

Result: The result is a rigorous and general tool named DataShifts, capable of quantifying distribution shifts and estimating the error bound in most practical applications, thereby advancing the analysis of learning error under distribution shift.

Conclusion: The conclusion is that this work significantly progresses the field by providing practical, theoretically grounded tools to analyze and mitigate learning errors under distribution shifts, bridging the gap between theoretical understanding and real-world applications.

Abstract: Generalization under distribution shift remains a core challenge in modern
machine learning, yet existing learning bound theory is limited to narrow,
idealized settings and is non-estimable from samples. In this paper, we bridge
the gap between theory and practical applications. We first show that existing
bounds become loose and non-estimable because their concept shift definition
breaks when the source and target supports mismatch. Leveraging entropic
optimal transport, we propose new support-agnostic definitions for covariate
and concept shifts, and derive a novel unified error bound that applies to
broad loss functions, label spaces, and stochastic labeling. We further develop
estimators for these shifts with concentration guarantees, and the DataShifts
algorithm, which can quantify distribution shifts and estimate the error bound
in most applications -- a rigorous and general tool for analyzing learning
error under distribution shift.

</details>


### [404] [Variational Learning Finds Flatter Solutions at the Edge of Stability](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12903)
*Avrajit Ghosh,Bai Cong,Rio Yokota,Saiprasad Ravishankar,Rongrong Wang,Molei Tao,Mohammad Emtiyaz Khan,Thomas Möllenhoff*

Main category: stat.ML

TL;DR: Variational Learning (VL) is a popular method for training deep neural networks. This paper analyzes the implicit regularization of VL through the Edge of Stability (EoS) framework, showing that VL can find flatter solutions by controlling posterior covariance and Monte Carlo samples. The findings are validated on large networks like ResNet and ViT.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To understand the implicit regularization in Variational Learning, which has shown empirical success but lacks theoretical analysis specifically addressing this aspect.

Method: The study extends the Edge of Stability (EoS) framework to Variational Learning. It involves controlling the posterior covariance and the number of Monte Carlo samples from the posterior to achieve flatter solutions. The approach begins with deriving results for a quadratic problem before extending it to deep neural networks.

Result: The theoretical results indicate that Variational Learning can find flatter solutions compared to standard methods. These findings are empirically validated across a variety of large networks, including ResNet and ViT, showing close alignment between theory and practice.

Conclusion: This work represents the first analysis of EoS dynamics within Variational Learning, providing insights into its implicit regularization mechanisms and confirming the ability of VL to discover flatter minima.

Abstract: Variational Learning (VL) has recently gained popularity for training deep
neural networks and is competitive to standard learning methods. Part of its
empirical success can be explained by theories such as PAC-Bayes bounds,
minimum description length and marginal likelihood, but there are few tools to
unravel the implicit regularization in play. Here, we analyze the implicit
regularization of VL through the Edge of Stability (EoS) framework. EoS has
previously been used to show that gradient descent can find flat solutions and
we extend this result to VL to show that it can find even flatter solutions.
This is obtained by controlling the posterior covariance and the number of
Monte Carlo samples from the posterior. These results are derived in a similar
fashion as the standard EoS literature for deep learning, by first deriving a
result for a quadratic problem and then extending it to deep neural networks.
We empirically validate these findings on a wide variety of large networks,
such as ResNet and ViT, to find that the theoretical results closely match the
empirical ones. Ours is the first work to analyze the EoS dynamics in VL.

</details>


### [405] [Random Matrix Theory for Deep Learning: Beyond Eigenvalues of Linear Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13139)
*Zhenyu Liao,Michael W. Mahoney*

Main category: stat.ML

TL;DR: The paper extends Random Matrix Theory to analyze nonlinear ML models like DNNs in the high-dimensional proportional regime, introducing High-dimensional Equivalent for a unified understanding of deep learning.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Modern ML and DNNs operate in high-dimensional spaces with overparameterized models, requiring new theoretical frameworks beyond classical low-dimensional intuitions.

Method: Introduces High-dimensional Equivalent to address technical challenges of high dimensionality, nonlinearity, and eigenspectral functionals in analyzing ML models.

Result: Provides precise characterizations of training and generalization performance for linear and nonlinear models, capturing phenomena such as scaling laws and double descent.

Conclusion: Offers a unified perspective on the theoretical understanding of deep learning in high dimensions.

Abstract: Modern Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) often operate on
high-dimensional data and rely on overparameterized models, where classical
low-dimensional intuitions break down. In particular, the proportional regime
where the data dimension, sample size, and number of model parameters are all
large and comparable, gives rise to novel and sometimes counterintuitive
behaviors. This paper extends traditional Random Matrix Theory (RMT) beyond
eigenvalue-based analysis of linear models to address the challenges posed by
nonlinear ML models such as DNNs in this regime. We introduce the concept of
High-dimensional Equivalent, which unifies and generalizes both Deterministic
Equivalent and Linear Equivalent, to systematically address three technical
challenges: high dimensionality, nonlinearity, and the need to analyze generic
eigenspectral functionals. Leveraging this framework, we provide precise
characterizations of the training and generalization performance of linear
models, nonlinear shallow networks, and deep networks. Our results capture rich
phenomena, including scaling laws, double descent, and nonlinear learning
dynamics, offering a unified perspective on the theoretical understanding of
deep learning in high dimensions.

</details>


### [406] [Experimental Design for Semiparametric Bandits](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13390)
*Seok-Jin Kim,Gi-Soo Kim,Min-hwan Oh*

Main category: stat.ML

TL;DR: 研究了有限臂半参数老虎机问题，提出了一种实验设计方法，该方法同时提供了尖锐的后悔界、PAC界和最佳臂识别保证。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 研究有限臂半参数老虎机问题，其中每个臂的奖励包含一个线性分量和一个未知的、可能对抗性的偏移。

Method: 提出了一种实验设计方法，通过正交化回归的精细非渐近分析，达到最优的$\sqrt{d}$速率。

Result: 该方法达到了最小最大后悔$\tilde{O}(\sqrt{dT})$，与已知的有限臂线性老虎机的下界匹配，并在正次优间隙条件下实现对数后悔。

Conclusion: 所提出的方法为广泛的半参数老虎机问题提供了强大且高效的學習保证。

Abstract: We study finite-armed semiparametric bandits, where each arm's reward
combines a linear component with an unknown, potentially adversarial shift.
This model strictly generalizes classical linear bandits and reflects
complexities common in practice. We propose the first experimental-design
approach that simultaneously offers a sharp regret bound, a PAC bound, and a
best-arm identification guarantee. Our method attains the minimax regret
$\tilde{O}(\sqrt{dT})$, matching the known lower bound for finite-armed linear
bandits, and further achieves logarithmic regret under a positive suboptimality
gap condition. These guarantees follow from our refined non-asymptotic analysis
of orthogonalized regression that attains the optimal $\sqrt{d}$ rate, paving
the way for robust and efficient learning across a broad class of
semiparametric bandit problems.

</details>


### [407] [Variational Inference with Mixtures of Isotropic Gaussians](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13613)
*Marguerite Petit-Talamon,Marc Lambert,Anna Korba*

Main category: stat.ML

TL;DR: The paper proposes a variational inference framework with efficient algorithms for approximating Bayesian posteriors using mixtures of isotropic Gaussians and uniform weights, balancing accuracy and computational efficiency.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Variational inference is widely used in Bayesian inference to approximate posterior distributions. However, existing methods may not balance well between approximation accuracy and computational efficiency when dealing with multimodal distributions.

Method: The method focuses on the parametric family of mixtures of isotropic Gaussians with diagonal covariance matrices proportional to the identity and uniform weights. It implements gradient descent on the location of mixture components and either Mirror or Bures descent on variance parameters.

Result: The developed algorithms show promising performance in numerical experiments, providing accurate approximations while maintaining memory and computational efficiency.

Conclusion: Mixtures of isotropic Gaussians with uniform weights offer an effective compromise between precise approximations of multimodal Bayesian posteriors and manageable computational resources.

Abstract: Variational inference (VI) is a popular approach in Bayesian inference, that
looks for the best approximation of the posterior distribution within a
parametric family, minimizing a loss that is typically the (reverse)
Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence. In this paper, we focus on the following
parametric family: mixtures of isotropic Gaussians (i.e., with diagonal
covariance matrices proportional to the identity) and uniform weights. We
develop a variational framework and provide efficient algorithms suited for
this family. In contrast with mixtures of Gaussian with generic covariance
matrices, this choice presents a balance between accurate approximations of
multimodal Bayesian posteriors, while being memory and computationally
efficient. Our algorithms implement gradient descent on the location of the
mixture components (the modes of the Gaussians), and either (an entropic)
Mirror or Bures descent on their variance parameters. We illustrate the
performance of our algorithms on numerical experiments.

</details>


### [408] [Exploiting the Exact Denoising Posterior Score in Training-Free Guidance of Diffusion Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13614)
*Gregory Bellchambers*

Main category: stat.ML

TL;DR: The paper introduces a novel expression for the exact posterior score in denoising tasks, analyzes errors in DPS scores, computes optimal step sizes, and demonstrates competitiveness with state-of-the-art techniques.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To improve conditional sampling via training-free guidance in diffusion models for image restoration and inverse problems by addressing limitations in current methods like Diffusion Posterior Sampling (DPS).

Method: Developed a new expression for the exact posterior score in purely denoising tasks, analyzed time-dependent error in DPS scores, and computed step sizes dynamically to minimize error at each step.

Result: Achieved competitive results with state-of-the-art techniques while requiring fewer time steps than DPS, and showed transferability of step sizes to related inverse problems such as colorization, random inpainting, and super resolution.

Conclusion: The proposed approach offers a simple yet effective alternative to existing methods, providing better performance with reduced computational requirements.

Abstract: The success of diffusion models has driven interest in performing conditional
sampling via training-free guidance of the denoising process to solve image
restoration and other inverse problems. A popular class of methods, based on
Diffusion Posterior Sampling (DPS), attempts to approximate the intractable
posterior score function directly. In this work, we present a novel expression
for the exact posterior score for purely denoising tasks that is tractable in
terms of the unconditional score function. We leverage this result to analyze
the time-dependent error in the DPS score for denoising tasks and compute step
sizes on the fly to minimize the error at each time step. We demonstrate that
these step sizes are transferable to related inverse problems such as
colorization, random inpainting, and super resolution. Despite its simplicity,
this approach is competitive with state-of-the-art techniques and enables
sampling with fewer time steps than DPS.

</details>


### [409] [Adversarial Disentanglement by Backpropagation with Physics-Informed Variational Autoencoder](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13658)
*Ioannis Christoforos Koune,Alice Cicirello*

Main category: stat.ML

TL;DR: 提出了一种物理信息变分自编码器架构，结合了基于物理模型的可解释性和数据驱动模型的灵活性。通过将潜在空间划分为物理意义变量和数据驱动变量，并采用对抗训练目标约束解码器，确保已知物理量的可解释性。该模型在合成案例研究中表现出色，能够分离已知物理和混淆影响。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 推理和预测部分已知物理系统的响应具有挑战性，特别是在多个混淆源影响测量结果时。基于物理的模型难以明确考虑这些影响，而数据驱动模型（如变分自编码器）不能保证找到简约表示，导致在有限且噪声数据下泛化性能差、重建精度低。

Method: 提出一种物理信息变分自编码器架构，将潜在空间划分为物理意义变量和数据驱动变量。物理意义变量用于参数化基于物理的模型，数据驱动变量捕捉系统领域和类别的变化。编码器与解码器耦合，解码器整合了基于物理和数据驱动的组件，并受对抗训练目标约束，以防止数据驱动组件覆盖已知物理，从而保持物理接地潜变量的可解释性。

Result: 模型能够分离输入信号的特征，并使用类别和领域可观测值的监督形式将已知物理与混淆影响分开。在一系列与工程结构相关的合成案例研究中，验证了该方法的可行性。

Conclusion: 提出的物理信息变分自编码器成功地结合了基于物理模型的可解释性和数据驱动模型的灵活性，能够在监督条件下分离已知物理和混淆影响，为工程结构相关问题提供了一种可行的新方法。

Abstract: Inference and prediction under partial knowledge of a physical system is
challenging, particularly when multiple confounding sources influence the
measured response. Explicitly accounting for these influences in physics-based
models is often infeasible due to epistemic uncertainty, cost, or time
constraints, resulting in models that fail to accurately describe the behavior
of the system. On the other hand, data-driven machine learning models such as
variational autoencoders are not guaranteed to identify a parsimonious
representation. As a result, they can suffer from poor generalization
performance and reconstruction accuracy in the regime of limited and noisy
data. We propose a physics-informed variational autoencoder architecture that
combines the interpretability of physics-based models with the flexibility of
data-driven models. To promote disentanglement of the known physics and
confounding influences, the latent space is partitioned into physically
meaningful variables that parametrize a physics-based model, and data-driven
variables that capture variability in the domain and class of the physical
system. The encoder is coupled with a decoder that integrates physics-based and
data-driven components, and constrained by an adversarial training objective
that prevents the data-driven components from overriding the known physics,
ensuring that the physics-grounded latent variables remain interpretable. We
demonstrate that the model is able to disentangle features of the input signal
and separate the known physics from confounding influences using supervision in
the form of class and domain observables. The model is evaluated on a series of
synthetic case studies relevant to engineering structures, demonstrating the
feasibility of the proposed approach.

</details>


### [410] [Understanding Learning Invariance in Deep Linear Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13714)
*Hao Duan,Guido Montúfar*

Main category: stat.ML

TL;DR: In this paper, the authors theoretically compare three approaches for achieving invariance in machine learning models: data augmentation, regularization, and hard-wiring.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Equivariant and invariant machine learning models can exploit symmetries and structural patterns in data to improve sample efficiency. However, theoretical insights into the performance of different methods to achieve invariance are limited.

Method: The authors focus on mean squared error regression with deep linear networks that parametrize rank-bounded linear maps and can be hard-wired to be invariant to specific group actions. They analyze the critical points of the optimization problems for hard-wiring and data augmentation, and contrast them with the effects of regularization.

Result: The critical points for hard-wiring and data augmentation are identical, consisting only of saddles and the global optimum. Regularization introduces additional critical points but they remain saddles except for the global optimum. The regularization path is continuous and converges to the hard-wired solution.

Conclusion: This theoretical analysis provides insights into the similarities and differences among the three invariance-achieving approaches, suggesting that regularization may serve as a smooth transition to hard-wired invariance.

Abstract: Equivariant and invariant machine learning models exploit symmetries and
structural patterns in data to improve sample efficiency. While empirical
studies suggest that data-driven methods such as regularization and data
augmentation can perform comparably to explicitly invariant models, theoretical
insights remain scarce. In this paper, we provide a theoretical comparison of
three approaches for achieving invariance: data augmentation, regularization,
and hard-wiring. We focus on mean squared error regression with deep linear
networks, which parametrize rank-bounded linear maps and can be hard-wired to
be invariant to specific group actions. We show that the critical points of the
optimization problems for hard-wiring and data augmentation are identical,
consisting solely of saddles and the global optimum. By contrast,
regularization introduces additional critical points, though they remain
saddles except for the global optimum. Moreover, we demonstrate that the
regularization path is continuous and converges to the hard-wired solution.

</details>

### [411] [Efficient Approximate Temporal Triangle Counting in Streaming with Predictions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13173)
*Giorgio Venturin,Ilie Sarpe,Fabio Vandin*

Main category: cs.DS

TL;DR: An algorithm named STEP is introduced to approximate temporal triangle counts in large-scale temporal graphs from a stream of temporal edges with scalability, efficiency, and accuracy.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing exact and approximate algorithms cannot handle large-scale temporal graphs efficiently due to their massive size with millions of nodes and billions of temporal edges. There's a need for an algorithm that can process these large graphs in a streaming manner while being resource-efficient.

Method: STEP combines predictions on the number of triangles each temporal edge is involved in with a simple sampling strategy, ensuring scalability, efficiency, and accurate approximation of all eight temporal triangle types simultaneously. It uses a sublinear amount of memory to obtain unbiased and accurate estimates.

Result: Theoretical analysis proves that STEP provides unbiased and highly accurate estimates even when using noisy predictions. Extensive experiments on massive temporal graphs show that STEP generates high-quality estimates and outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of efficiency.

Conclusion: STEP is a scalable and efficient algorithm for approximating temporal triangle counts in large-scale temporal graphs, providing high-quality estimates with less memory usage.

Abstract: Triangle counting is a fundamental and widely studied problem on static
graphs, and recently on temporal graphs, where edges carry information on the
timings of the associated events. Streaming processing and resource efficiency
are crucial requirements for counting triangles in modern massive temporal
graphs, with millions of nodes and up to billions of temporal edges. However,
current exact and approximate algorithms are unable to handle large-scale
temporal graphs. To fill such a gap, we introduce STEP, a scalable and
efficient algorithm to approximate temporal triangle counts from a stream of
temporal edges. STEP combines predictions to the number of triangles a temporal
edge is involved in, with a simple sampling strategy, leading to scalability,
efficiency, and accurate approximation of all eight temporal triangle types
simultaneously. We analytically prove that, by using a sublinear amount of
memory, STEP obtains unbiased and very accurate estimates. In fact, even noisy
predictions can significantly reduce the variance of STEP's estimates. Our
extensive experiments on massive temporal graphs with up to billions of edges
demonstrate that STEP outputs high-quality estimates and is more efficient than
state-of-the-art methods.

</details>


<div id='cs.PL'></div>

# cs.PL [[Back]](#toc)

### [412] [A Fast, Reliable, and Secure Programming Language for LLM Agents with Code Actions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12202)
*Stephen Mell,Botong Zhang,David Mell,Shuo Li,Ramya Ramalingam,Nathan Yu,Steve Zdancewic,Osbert Bastani*

Main category: cs.PL

TL;DR: A new programming language Quasar is proposed for code actions of LLMs, which can improve performance, security and reliability. Experiments show that LLMs with Quasar actions retain strong performance, reduce execution time by 42%, improve security by 52% and improve reliability.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Modern large language models (LLMs) are often deployed as agents calling external tools adaptively to solve tasks. Writing code instead of directly calling tools enables them to automatically generate complex control flow such as conditionals and loops. However, Python may not be the ideal language due to limited built-in support for performance, security, and reliability.

Method: Propose a novel programming language Quasar for code actions, which has automated parallelization, uncertainty quantification and security features. LLMs can write code in a subset of Python, which is automatically transpiled to Quasar.

Result: On the ViperGPT visual question answering agent applied to the GQA dataset, LLMs with Quasar actions instead of Python actions retain strong performance, while reducing execution time when possible by 42%, improving security by reducing user approval interactions when possible by 52%, and improving reliability by applying conformal prediction to achieve a desired target coverage level.

Conclusion: Quasar is a promising programming language for code actions of LLMs, which can improve performance, security and reliability.

Abstract: Modern large language models (LLMs) are often deployed as agents, calling
external tools adaptively to solve tasks. Rather than directly calling tools,
it can be more effective for LLMs to write code to perform the tool calls,
enabling them to automatically generate complex control flow such as
conditionals and loops. Such code actions are typically provided as Python
code, since LLMs are quite proficient at it; however, Python may not be the
ideal language due to limited built-in support for performance, security, and
reliability. We propose a novel programming language for code actions, called
Quasar, which has several benefits: (1) automated parallelization to improve
performance, (2) uncertainty quantification to improve reliability and mitigate
hallucinations, and (3) security features enabling the user to validate
actions. LLMs can write code in a subset of Python, which is automatically
transpiled to Quasar. We evaluate our approach on the ViperGPT visual question
answering agent, applied to the GQA dataset, demonstrating that LLMs with
Quasar actions instead of Python actions retain strong performance, while
reducing execution time when possible by 42%, improving security by reducing
user approval interactions when possible by 52%, and improving reliability by
applying conformal prediction to achieve a desired target coverage level.

</details>


<div id='cs.NI'></div>

# cs.NI [[Back]](#toc)

### [413] [Multi-domain anomaly detection in a 5G network](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12070)
*Thomas Hoger,Philippe Owezarski*

Main category: cs.NI

TL;DR: To address the increased attack surface in dynamic 5G mobile networks, this paper proposes a multi-domain anomaly detection method.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: With the advent of 5G, mobile networks are becoming more dynamic and will therefore present a wider attack surface.

Method: The proposed method studies traffic correlation on three dimensions: temporal by analyzing message sequences, semantic by abstracting the parameters these messages contain, and topological by linking them in the form of a graph.

Result: Unlike traditional approaches which consider domains independently, the proposed method provides a global, coherent and explainable view of anomalies.

Conclusion: A multi-domain anomaly detection method that considers correlations between temporal, semantic, and topological dimensions is proposed to secure dynamic 5G mobile networks.

Abstract: With the advent of 5G, mobile networks are becoming more dynamic and will
therefore present a wider attack surface. To secure these new systems, we
propose a multi-domain anomaly detection method that is distinguished by the
study of traffic correlation on three dimensions: temporal by analyzing message
sequences, semantic by abstracting the parameters these messages contain, and
topological by linking them in the form of a graph. Unlike traditional
approaches, which are limited to considering these domains independently, our
method studies their correlations to obtain a global, coherent and explainable
view of anomalies.

</details>


### [414] [Latency Optimization for Wireless Federated Learning in Multihop Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12081)
*Shaba Shaon,Van-Dinh Nguyen,Dinh C. Nguyen*

Main category: cs.NI

TL;DR: The paper focuses on minimizing latency in wireless federated learning over multi-hop networks via a personalized learning and adaptive aggregation-aware FL (PAFL) framework, presenting an optimization problem solved with block coordinate descent and SCA techniques.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the issue of high latency in wireless federated learning across multi-hop networks due to data heterogeneity and inefficient node utilization.

Method: A PAFL framework is proposed which optimizes the operations of leaf and relay nodes along with relay routing indicators. The method incorporates energy harvesting for relay nodes and solves a complex optimization problem using block coordinate descent and successive convex approximation techniques.

Result: Simulation results show that the proposed joint optimization approach significantly reduces system latency by up to 69.37% compared to other schemes such as those optimizing only one node type or traditional greedy algorithms.

Conclusion: The PAFL framework effectively minimizes latency in wireless multi-hop federated learning systems through efficient coordination of leaf and relay nodes and the inclusion of relay routing indicators.

Abstract: In this paper, we study a novel latency minimization problem in wireless
federated learning (FL) across multi-hop networks. The system comprises
multiple routes, each integrating leaf and relay nodes for FL model training.
We explore a personalized learning and adaptive aggregation-aware FL (PAFL)
framework that effectively addresses data heterogeneity across participating
nodes by harmonizing individual and collective learning objectives. We
formulate an optimization problem aimed at minimizing system latency through
the joint optimization of leaf and relay nodes, as well as relay routing
indicator. We also incorporate an additional energy harvesting scheme for the
relay nodes to help with their relay tasks. This formulation presents a
computationally demanding challenge, and thus we develop a simple yet efficient
algorithm based on block coordinate descent and successive convex approximation
(SCA) techniques. Simulation results illustrate the efficacy of our proposed
joint optimization approach for leaf and relay nodes with relay routing
indicator. We observe significant latency savings in the wireless multi-hop
PAFL system, with reductions of up to 69.37% compared to schemes optimizing
only one node type, traditional greedy algorithm, and scheme without relay
routing indicator.

</details>


### [415] [Learning Best Paths in Quantum Networks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12462)
*Xuchuang Wang,Maoli Liu,Xutong Liu,Zhuohua Li,Mohammad Hajiesmaili,John C. S. Lui,Don Towsley*

Main category: cs.NI

TL;DR: 本论文研究了在量子网络中在线学习最佳路径的方法，提出了两种算法BeQuP-Link和BeQuP-Path，分别适用于不同反馈类型的量子网络，并通过NetSquid模拟验证了其准确性和高效性。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 量子网络传输易受噪声影响的量子信息，而许多关键应用（如量子密钥分发和分布式量子计算）依赖于高效的量子信息传输，因此需要一种有效的方法来学习量子网络中最佳路径以提升这些应用性能。

Method: 论文探讨了两种反馈类型：链路级反馈和路径级反馈，并提出了两种在线学习算法BeQuP-Link和BeQuP-Path。BeQuP-Link通过动态基准测试关键链路来识别最佳路径；BeQuP-Path则通过子程序将路径级观察结果转换为估计链路级参数，从而确定最佳路径。

Result: 理论分析表明，这两种算法都能高效且大概率地确定最佳路径。此外，基于NetSquid的模拟实验验证了这两种算法能够准确、高效地识别最佳路径。

Conclusion: 论文提出的两种在线学习算法BeQuP-Link和BeQuP-Path分别适用于具有不同类型反馈的量子网络，并且能够在理论上和实践中有效地确定最佳路径，为提升量子网络应用性能提供了新方法。

Abstract: Quantum networks (QNs) transmit delicate quantum information across noisy
quantum channels. Crucial applications, like quantum key distribution (QKD) and
distributed quantum computation (DQC), rely on efficient quantum information
transmission. Learning the best path between a pair of end nodes in a QN is key
to enhancing such applications. This paper addresses learning the best path in
a QN in the online learning setting. We explore two types of feedback:
"link-level" and "path-level". Link-level feedback pertains to QNs with
advanced quantum switches that enable link-level benchmarking. Path-level
feedback, on the other hand, is associated with basic quantum switches that
permit only path-level benchmarking. We introduce two online learning
algorithms, BeQuP-Link and BeQuP-Path, to identify the best path using
link-level and path-level feedback, respectively. To learn the best path,
BeQuP-Link benchmarks the critical links dynamically, while BeQuP-Path relies
on a subroutine, transferring path-level observations to estimate link-level
parameters in a batch manner. We analyze the quantum resource complexity of
these algorithms and demonstrate that both can efficiently and, with high
probability, determine the best path. Finally, we perform NetSquid-based
simulations and validate that both algorithms accurately and efficiently
identify the best path.

</details>


### [416] [Dynamic Preference Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning for Internet Network Management](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13153)
*DongNyeong Heo,Daniela Noemi Rim,Heeyoul Choi*

Main category: cs.NI

TL;DR: A new RL-based network management method is proposed, which allows agents to select actions based on states and preferences, and a numerical method for estimating preference distribution is also proposed.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current RL algorithms optimize agents with respect to a single static reward formulation. However, in practice, the preference could vary according to network status, external concerns and so on.

Method: Propose new RL-based network management agents that can select actions based on both states and preferences, and a numerical method that can estimate the distribution of preference.

Result: Experiment results show that the RL agents trained based on the proposed approach significantly generalize better with various preferences than the previous RL approaches. Several analyses demonstrate the advantages of the numerical estimation method.

Conclusion: The proposed RL-based network management agents can generalize on various states and preferences, and the numerical method for estimating preference distribution is advantageous for unbiased training.

Abstract: An internet network service provider manages its network with multiple
objectives, such as high quality of service (QoS) and minimum computing
resource usage. To achieve these objectives, a reinforcement learning-based
(RL) algorithm has been proposed to train its network management agent.
Usually, their algorithms optimize their agents with respect to a single static
reward formulation consisting of multiple objectives with fixed importance
factors, which we call preferences. However, in practice, the preference could
vary according to network status, external concerns and so on. For example,
when a server shuts down and it can cause other servers' traffic overloads
leading to additional shutdowns, it is plausible to reduce the preference of
QoS while increasing the preference of minimum computing resource usages. In
this paper, we propose new RL-based network management agents that can select
actions based on both states and preferences. With our proposed approach, we
expect a single agent to generalize on various states and preferences.
Furthermore, we propose a numerical method that can estimate the distribution
of preference that is advantageous for unbiased training. Our experiment
results show that the RL agents trained based on our proposed approach
significantly generalize better with various preferences than the previous RL
approaches, which assume static preference during training. Moreover, we
demonstrate several analyses that show the advantages of our numerical
estimation method.

</details>


<div id='eess.SY'></div>

# eess.SY [[Back]](#toc)

### [417] [Nonlinear Model Order Reduction of Dynamical Systems in Process Engineering: Review and Comparison](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12819)
*Jan C. Schulze,Alexander Mitsos*

Main category: eess.SY

TL;DR: To enable real-time applications, this paper reviews and compares state-of-the-art nonlinear model order reduction methods, extends manifold-Galerkin approaches for dynamical systems with inputs, and applies eight established methods to an air separation process model.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Computationally cheap yet accurate enough dynamical models are crucial for real-time capable nonlinear optimization and model-based control.

Method: The authors review and compare state-of-the-art nonlinear model order reduction methods, extend manifold-Galerkin approaches to dynamical systems with inputs, and apply eight established methods to an air separation process model.

Result: The comparative case study provides insights into the strengths and weaknesses of each method, highlighting their applicability and limitations in reducing complex models for real-time applications.

Conclusion: Nonlinear model order reduction methods have varying strengths and weaknesses. The extended manifold-Galerkin approach and other reviewed methods can facilitate real-time applications in nonlinear optimization and model-based control.

Abstract: Computationally cheap yet accurate enough dynamical models are vital for
real-time capable nonlinear optimization and model-based control. When given a
computationally expensive high-order prediction model, a reduction to a
lower-order simplified model can enable such real-time applications. Herein, we
review state-of-the-art nonlinear model order reduction methods and provide a
theoretical comparison of method properties. Additionally, we discuss both
general-purpose methods and tailored approaches for (chemical) process systems
and we identify similarities and differences between these methods. As
manifold-Galerkin approaches currently do not account for inputs in the
construction of the reduced state subspace, we extend these methods to
dynamical systems with inputs. In a comparative case study, we apply eight
established model order reduction methods to an air separation process model:
POD-Galerkin, nonlinear-POD-Galerkin, manifold-Galerkin, dynamic mode
decomposition, Koopman theory, manifold learning with latent predictor,
compartment modeling, and model aggregation. Herein, we do not investigate
hyperreduction (reduction of FLOPS). Based on our findings, we discuss
strengths and weaknesses of the model order reduction methods.

</details>


### [418] [Condition Monitoring with Machine Learning: A Data-Driven Framework for Quantifying Wind Turbine Energy Loss](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13012)
*Emil Marcus Buchberg,Kent Vugs Nielsen*

Main category: eess.SY

TL;DR: Wind energy is important but faces operational challenges. This study proposes a scalable machine learning framework for condition monitoring of wind turbines, reducing data and detecting anomalies effectively.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the issue of Leading-Edge Erosion on wind turbine blades which reduces energy output, the study aims to improve anomaly detection using SCADA data.

Method: The framework preprocesses data rigorously, applies domain-specific rules and anomaly detection filters (like Gaussian Mixture Models), and uses a predictive power score. Data cleaning and feature selection help identify performance degradation.

Result: Data preprocessing reduced data significantly, retaining 31% of original SCADA data per wind farm. Detected clear performance declines in 24 out of 35 turbines, improvements in seven, and no changes in four. Models like Random Forest, XGBoost, and KNN captured persistent declines in turbine performance.

Conclusion: The developed machine learning framework offers a new approach to condition monitoring by isolating normal operational data and estimating annual energy loss, potentially reducing maintenance costs.

Abstract: Wind energy significantly contributes to the global shift towards renewable
energy, yet operational challenges, such as Leading-Edge Erosion on wind
turbine blades, notably reduce energy output. This study introduces an
advanced, scalable machine learning framework for condition monitoring of wind
turbines, specifically targeting improved detection of anomalies using
Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition data. The framework effectively
isolates normal turbine behavior through rigorous preprocessing, incorporating
domain-specific rules and anomaly detection filters, including Gaussian Mixture
Models and a predictive power score. The data cleaning and feature selection
process enables identification of deviations indicative of performance
degradation, facilitating estimates of annual energy production losses. The
data preprocessing methods resulted in significant data reduction, retaining on
average 31% of the original SCADA data per wind farm. Notably, 24 out of 35
turbines exhibited clear performance declines. At the same time, seven
improved, and four showed no significant changes when employing the power curve
feature set, which consisted of wind speed and ambient temperature. Models such
as Random Forest, XGBoost, and KNN consistently captured subtle but persistent
declines in turbine performance. The developed framework provides a novel
approach to existing condition monitoring methodologies by isolating normal
operational data and estimating annual energy loss, which can be a key part in
reducing maintenance expenditures and mitigating economic impacts from turbine
downtime.

</details>


### [419] [A Hybrid Artificial Intelligence Method for Estimating Flicker in Power Systems](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13611)
*Javad Enayati,Pedram Asef,Alexandre Benoit*

Main category: eess.SY

TL;DR: A new hybrid AI method for flicker component estimation in power distribution systems is presented, which combines H filtering and an adaptive linear neuron network. This approach offers better accuracy, robustness, and less computational load compared to existing methods like Fast Fourier Transform and Discrete Wavelet Transform based estimators.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To improve the estimation of flicker components in power distribution systems, especially under uncertain and noisy conditions, where traditional frequency domain approaches have limitations such as slow convergence and sensitivity to noise.

Method: The method uses H filtering to extract the voltage envelope under uncertain and noisy conditions, then applies ADALINE to identify flicker frequencies embedded in the envelope. This hybrid AI model does not require prior knowledge of noise characteristics or extensive training.

Result: Simulation studies based on IEC Standard 61000-4-15, statistical analysis, Monte Carlo simulations, and real-world data demonstrate superior accuracy, robustness, and reduced computational load compared to Fast Fourier Transform and Discrete Wavelet Transform based estimators.

Conclusion: The novel hybrid AI method combining H filtering and an adaptive linear neuron network provides a more effective solution for flicker component estimation in power distribution systems.

Abstract: This paper introduces a novel hybrid AI method combining H filtering and an
adaptive linear neuron network for flicker component estimation in power
distribution systems.The proposed method leverages the robustness of the H
filter to extract the voltage envelope under uncertain and noisy conditions
followed by the use of ADALINE to accurately identify flicker frequencies
embedded in the envelope.This synergy enables efficient time domain estimation
with rapid convergence and noise resilience addressing key limitations of
existing frequency domain approaches.Unlike conventional techniques this hybrid
AI model handles complex power disturbances without prior knowledge of noise
characteristics or extensive training.To validate the method performance we
conduct simulation studies based on IEC Standard 61000 4 15 supported by
statistical analysis Monte Carlo simulations and real world data.Results
demonstrate superior accuracy robustness and reduced computational load
compared to Fast Fourier Transform and Discrete Wavelet Transform based
estimators.

</details>


<div id='cs.AR'></div>

# cs.AR [[Back]](#toc)

### [420] [PuDHammer: Experimental Analysis of Read Disturbance Effects of Processing-using-DRAM in Real DRAM Chips](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12947)
*Ismail Emir Yuksel,Akash Sood,Ataberk Olgun,Oğuzhan Canpolat,Haocong Luo,F. Nisa Bostancı,Mohammad Sadrosadati,A. Giray Yağlıkçı,Onur Mutlu*

Main category: cs.AR

TL;DR: The paper investigates the effects of multiple-row activation on DRAM read disturbance in Processing-using-DRAM (PuD) operations, presenting a study named PuDHammer. It significantly worsens read disturbance vulnerability compared to RowHammer and bypasses existing mitigation mechanisms. The authors propose three countermeasures and adapt PRAC for mitigating these issues, but the adapted solution incurs substantial performance overheads.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To understand and address the potential risks and vulnerabilities associated with Processing-using-DRAM (PuD) operations, specifically focusing on the impact of multiple-row activation on DRAM read disturbance which has not been explored before.

Method: The researchers conducted an extensive characterization study using 316 real DDR4 DRAM chips from four major manufacturers. They analyzed the read disturbance effects under various operational conditions and parameters, comparing PuDHammer with RowHammer. Additionally, they developed three countermeasures and adapted PRAC for mitigating the identified vulnerabilities.

Result: PuDHammer significantly increases read disturbance vulnerability, reducing the minimum hammer count required for the first bitflip by up to 158.58x compared to RowHammer. Combining RowHammer with PuDHammer reduces the hammer count further. PuDHammer bypasses existing RowHammer mitigation mechanisms. The adapted PRAC incurs large performance overheads.

Conclusion: PuDHammer poses serious threats to DRAM reliability. Future robust PuD-enabled systems need effective countermeasures as current solutions like adapted PRAC are insufficient due to high performance costs.

Abstract: Processing-using-DRAM (PuD) is a promising paradigm for alleviating the data
movement bottleneck using DRAM's massive internal parallelism and bandwidth to
execute very wide operations. Performing a PuD operation involves activating
multiple DRAM rows in quick succession or simultaneously, i.e., multiple-row
activation. Multiple-row activation is fundamentally different from
conventional memory access patterns that activate one DRAM row at a time.
However, repeatedly activating even one DRAM row (e.g., RowHammer) can induce
bitflips in unaccessed DRAM rows because modern DRAM is subject to read
disturbance. Unfortunately, no prior work investigates the effects of
multiple-row activation on DRAM read disturbance.
  In this paper, we present the first characterization study of read
disturbance effects of multiple-row activation-based PuD (which we call
PuDHammer) using 316 real DDR4 DRAM chips from four major DRAM manufacturers.
Our detailed characterization show that 1) PuDHammer significantly exacerbates
the read disturbance vulnerability, causing up to 158.58x reduction in the
minimum hammer count required to induce the first bitflip ($HC_{first}$),
compared to RowHammer, 2) PuDHammer is affected by various operational
conditions and parameters, 3) combining RowHammer with PuDHammer is more
effective than using RowHammer alone to induce read disturbance error, e.g.,
doing so reduces $HC_{first}$ by 1.66x on average, and 4) PuDHammer bypasses an
in-DRAM RowHammer mitigation mechanism (Target Row Refresh) and induces more
bitflips than RowHammer.
  To develop future robust PuD-enabled systems in the presence of PuDHammer, we
1) develop three countermeasures and 2) adapt and evaluate the state-of-the-art
RowHammer mitigation standardized by industry, called Per Row Activation
Counting (PRAC). We show that the adapted PRAC incurs large performance
overheads (48.26%, on average).

</details>


<div id='physics.comp-ph'></div>

# physics.comp-ph [[Back]](#toc)

### [421] [Latent Representation Learning of Multi-scale Thermophysics: Application to Dynamics in Shocked Porous Energetic Material](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12996)
*Shahab Azarfar,Joseph B. Choi,Phong CH. Nguyen,Yen T. Nguyen,Pradeep Seshadri,H. S. Udaykumar,Stephen Baek*

Main category: physics.comp-ph

TL;DR: This paper explores a meta-learning approach for multi-scale modeling in microstructured materials, using tokenization to learn reduced representations of micro-scale physics to accelerate meso-scale learning. The model outperforms PARC with limited meso-scale data.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Meso-scale simulations for training deep learning models are computationally expensive. There is a need for an alternative method that can reduce the computational cost while maintaining or improving accuracy.

Method: A meta-learning approach inspired by tokenization in natural language processing is used. A probabilistic latent representation of micro-scale dynamics serves as building blocks for meso-scale dynamics. Correlation between neighboring building blocks is learned through training on a small meso-scale dataset.

Result: The proposed model outperforms a physics-aware recurrent convolutional neural network (PARC) when trained with scarce meso-scale data.

Conclusion: The meta-learning approach accelerates the development of closure models by utilizing inexpensive micro-scale simulations and fast training over a small meso-scale dataset. This method has potential applications across various multi-scale modeling problems.

Abstract: Coupling of physics across length and time scales plays an important role in
the response of microstructured materials to external loads. In a multi-scale
framework, unresolved (subgrid) meso-scale dynamics is upscaled to the
homogenized (macro-scale) representation of the heterogeneous material through
closure models. Deep learning models trained using meso-scale simulation data
are now a popular route to assimilate such closure laws. However, meso-scale
simulations are computationally taxing, posing practical challenges in training
deep learning-based surrogate models from scratch. In this work, we investigate
an alternative meta-learning approach motivated by the idea of tokenization in
natural language processing. We show that one can learn a reduced
representation of the micro-scale physics to accelerate the meso-scale learning
process by tokenizing the meso-scale evolution of the physical fields involved
in an archetypal, albeit complex, reactive dynamics problem, \textit{viz.},
shock-induced energy localization in a porous energetic material. A
probabilistic latent representation of \textit{micro}-scale dynamics is learned
as building blocks for \textit{meso}-scale dynamics. The \textit{meso-}scale
latent dynamics model learns the correlation between neighboring building
blocks by training over a small dataset of meso-scale simulations. We compare
the performance of our model with a physics-aware recurrent convolutional
neural network (PARC) trained only on the full meso-scale dataset. We
demonstrate that our model can outperform PARC with scarce meso-scale data. The
proposed approach accelerates the development of closure models by leveraging
inexpensive micro-scale simulations and fast training over a small meso-scale
dataset, and can be applied to a range of multi-scale modeling problems.

</details>


<div id='cond-mat.mtrl-sci'></div>

# cond-mat.mtrl-sci [[Back]](#toc)

### [422] [Information fusion strategy integrating pre-trained language model and contrastive learning for materials knowledge mining](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12516)
*Yongqian Peng,Zhouran Zhang,Longhui Zhang,Fengyuan Zhao,Yahao Li,Yicong Ye,Shuxin Bai*

Main category: cond-mat.mtrl-sci

TL;DR: 机器学习在材料设计领域带来了革命性的变化，但预测诸如合金延展性等复杂属性仍然具有挑战性。本文提出了一种创新的信息融合架构，结合了材料科学文献中的领域特定文本与定量物理描述符，并通过MatSciBERT和对比学习方法自动提取关于加工参数和微观结构特性的隐含知识。该模型在钛合金和难熔多主元素合金数据集上表现出色，R2值分别为0.849和0.680，为复杂材料系统的属性预测提供了全面的框架。


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: 尽管机器学习在材料设计中取得了显著进展，但在预测复杂属性（如合金延展性）方面仍存在困难，这主要归因于加工条件和难以通过传统还原方法量化的微观结构特征的影响。

Method: 提出了一种信息融合架构，整合了材料科学文献中的领域特定文本和定量物理描述符。使用MatSciBERT进行高级文本理解，并采用对比学习方法自动提取关于加工参数和微观结构特性的隐含知识。

Result: 通过严格的消融研究和比较实验，该模型在钛合金验证集上达到了0.849的R2值，在难熔多主元素合金测试集上达到了0.680的R2值，表明其性能优越。

Conclusion: 该系统方法为复杂材料系统中的属性预测提供了一个全面的框架，特别是在定量描述符不完整的情况下，并为知识引导的材料设计和信息驱动的材料发现奠定了基础。

Abstract: Machine learning has revolutionized materials design, yet predicting complex
properties like alloy ductility remains challenging due to the influence of
processing conditions and microstructural features that resist quantification
through traditional reductionist approaches. Here, we present an innovative
information fusion architecture that integrates domain-specific texts from
materials science literature with quantitative physical descriptors to overcome
these limitations. Our framework employs MatSciBERT for advanced textual
comprehension and incorporates contrastive learning to automatically extract
implicit knowledge regarding processing parameters and microstructural
characteristics. Through rigorous ablation studies and comparative experiments,
the model demonstrates superior performance, achieving coefficient of
determination (R2) values of 0.849 and 0.680 on titanium alloy validation set
and refractory multi-principal-element alloy test set. This systematic approach
provides a holistic framework for property prediction in complex material
systems where quantitative descriptors are incomplete and establishes a
foundation for knowledge-guided materials design and informatics-driven
materials discovery.

</details>


### [423] [Language Models Enable Data-Augmented Synthesis Planning for Inorganic Materials](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12557)
*Thorben Prein,Elton Pan,Janik Jehkul,Steffen Weinmann,Elsa A. Olivetti,Jennifer L. M. Rupp*

Main category: cond-mat.mtrl-sci

TL;DR: Inorganic synthesis planning relies on heuristics or machine learning with limited datasets. Language models (without task-specific tuning) can predict synthesis conditions, achieving up to 53.8% Top-1 accuracy and 66.1% Top-5 accuracy for precursor prediction, and predict calcination/sintering temperatures with mean absolute errors below 126°C. Ensembling these models enhances accuracy and reduces cost by up to 70%. Using language models-generated recipes and literature-mined examples, a transformer-based model SyntMTE was pretrained and fine-tuned, reducing sintering temperature prediction error to 73°C and calcination to 98°C. This approach improves models by up to 8.7% compared to baselines. A case study on Li7La3Zr2O12 solid-state electrolytes shows SyntMTE reproduces dopant-dependent sintering trends. The hybrid workflow enables scalable inorganic synthesis planning.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current inorganic synthesis planning methods are constrained by heuristic approaches or machine-learning models trained on limited datasets, which limits their generality. There is a need for more scalable and data-efficient methods.

Method: The study uses off-the-shelf language models to predict synthesis conditions without task-specific fine-tuning. These models predict precursors and temperatures for inorganic reactions. The predictions are then used along with literature-mined examples to pretrain a transformer-based model called SyntMTE, which is subsequently fine-tuned on the combined dataset.

Result: The language models achieve a Top-1 precursor-prediction accuracy of up to 53.8% and a Top-5 performance of 66.1%. They also predict calcination and sintering temperatures with mean absolute errors below 126°C. After fine-tuning, SyntMTE reduces mean-absolute error in sintering temperature prediction to 73°C and in calcination temperature to 98°C, improving models by up to 8.7% compared to baselines.

Conclusion: This hybrid workflow combining language models and a transformer-based model enables scalable, data-efficient inorganic synthesis planning.

Abstract: Inorganic synthesis planning currently relies primarily on heuristic
approaches or machine-learning models trained on limited datasets, which
constrains its generality. We demonstrate that language models, without
task-specific fine-tuning, can recall synthesis conditions. Off-the-shelf
models, such as GPT-4.1, Gemini 2.0 Flash and Llama 4 Maverick, achieve a Top-1
precursor-prediction accuracy of up to 53.8 % and a Top-5 performance of 66.1 %
on a held-out set of 1,000 reactions. They also predict calcination and
sintering temperatures with mean absolute errors below 126 {\deg}C, matching
specialized regression methods. Ensembling these language models further
enhances predictive accuracy and reduces inference cost per prediction by up to
70 %. We subsequently employ language models to generate 28,548 synthetic
reaction recipes, which we combine with literature-mined examples to pretrain a
transformer-based model, SyntMTE. After fine-tuning on the combined dataset,
SyntMTE reduces mean-absolute error in sintering temperature prediction to 73
{\deg}C and in calcination temperature to 98 {\deg}C. This strategy improves
models by up to 8.7 % compared with baselines trained exclusively on
experimental data. Finally, in a case study on Li7La3Zr2O12 solid-state
electrolytes, we demonstrate that SyntMTE reproduces the experimentally
observed dopant-dependent sintering trends. Our hybrid workflow enables
scalable, data-efficient inorganic synthesis planning.

</details>


<div id='cs.GT'></div>

# cs.GT [[Back]](#toc)

### [424] [The impact of uncertainty on regularized learning in games](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.13286)
*Pierre-Louis Cauvin,Davide Legacci,Panayotis Mertikopoulos*

Main category: cs.GT

TL;DR: This paper explores how randomness and uncertainty affect learning in games, focusing on a perturbed version of FTRL dynamics. It finds that uncertainty drives players' strategies towards pure strategies, with pure Nash equilibria as the only possible limits. In games with recurrent deterministic dynamics, randomness causes the stochastic dynamics to drift towards the boundary.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To understand the impact of randomness and uncertainty on learning dynamics in games, particularly within the framework of FTRL where players experience random shocks in payoff observations and strategy updates.

Method: Analysis of a perturbed variant of FTRL dynamics under conditions of continuous random shocks, examining the trajectory of play towards pure strategies and identifying stable sets of pure strategies.

Result: Players' strategies reach arbitrarily close to pure strategies in finite time, even if they do not settle there permanently. The only possible limits of the dynamics are pure Nash equilibria, and stability requires closure under better replies. In games with recurrent deterministic dynamics, randomness leads to an average drift towards the boundary.

Conclusion: Uncertainty in game learning dynamics favors extreme (pure) strategies over mixed ones, with pure Nash equilibria emerging as robust predictions. Randomness disrupts recurrent behavior in certain games, pushing dynamics towards boundaries.

Abstract: In this paper, we investigate how randomness and uncertainty influence
learning in games. Specifically, we examine a perturbed variant of the dynamics
of "follow-the-regularized-leader" (FTRL), where the players' payoff
observations and strategy updates are continually impacted by random shocks.
Our findings reveal that, in a fairly precise sense, "uncertainty favors
extremes": in any game, regardless of the noise level, every player's
trajectory of play reaches an arbitrarily small neighborhood of a pure strategy
in finite time (which we estimate). Moreover, even if the player does not
ultimately settle at this strategy, they return arbitrarily close to some
(possibly different) pure strategy infinitely often. This prompts the question
of which sets of pure strategies emerge as robust predictions of learning under
uncertainty. We show that (a) the only possible limits of the FTRL dynamics
under uncertainty are pure Nash equilibria; and (b) a span of pure strategies
is stable and attracting if and only if it is closed under better replies.
Finally, we turn to games where the deterministic dynamics are recurrent - such
as zero-sum games with interior equilibria - and we show that randomness
disrupts this behavior, causing the stochastic dynamics to drift toward the
boundary on average.

</details>


<div id='cs.DC'></div>

# cs.DC [[Back]](#toc)

### [425] [Self-Stabilizing Replicated State Machine Coping with Byzantine and Recurring Transient Faults](https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12900)
*Shlomi Dolev,Amit Hendin,Maurice Herlihy,Maria Potop Butucaru,Elad Michael Schiller*

Main category: cs.DC

TL;DR: This paper introduces a protocol for repeated Byzantine agreement which satisfies key properties including Byzantine fault-tolerance, recurrent transient fault-tolerance, accuracy, and self-stabilization.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
